The operator, WCI, Inc., sued the Ohio Liquor Control Commission and Department of Public Safety to recover a $25,000 fine it paid under protest after state officials treated a dancer's nudity as a liquor permit violation.

The Ohio Liquor Control Commission revoked the liquor permit effective Sept. 20, 2018, after an Ohio Investigative Unit investigation in which agents bought drugs and lap dances with food stamp benefits.
The Montgomery County Prosecutor announced the club had been shut down after his office sought a preliminary injunction; 11 people faced sex, drug and food stamp charges.
Lost its liquor license in May 2018.
Raided in 2017. The Ohio State Highway Patrol said it was charged, along with The Harem and Sharkey's, in an administrative case before the Ohio Liquor Control Commission.
The Ohio Division of Liquor Control rejected the operator's liquor permit renewal, finding it had operated in disregard of state laws and local ordinances. The decision was appealable.
A homicide occurred in the club's parking lot in 2017, per WHIO.
Described as closed in January 2020 news coverage.
WTOL reported the club is named in a civil lawsuit and in two criminal cases arising from two drunk-driving crashes that killed three people.
Akron City Council unanimously passed a resolution objecting to renewal of the club's liquor permit after dozens of police calls; the city prosecutor also objected. Year to confirm.
Listed (as X Gentleman's club) on the Columbus City Attorney's liquor permit objection list sent to City Council for a vote. Date to confirm.

In Hart v. Rick's Cabaret, a federal judge in New York awarded about $10.9 million to a class of dancers after finding the club had misclassified them as independent contractors. History (older than 5 years).

A federal jury convicted the club's owner of sex trafficking conspiracy, bribery of a DEA agent, maintaining a drug-involved premises, narcotics conspiracy, witness tampering and cocaine distribution. Prosecutors said drugs and coercion were used to force dancers into sex acts inside the club.
The owner was sentenced to 25 years in federal prison.
Closed after its temporary liquor license expired following the owner's convictions.
